correctness.rationale: For n at least three, the two leaves force both leaves positive at any hypothetical weight below four; they must then both be label 1, after which the nested neighborhoods of a_{n-1} and b_2 contradict the Italian sum condition. At weight four, the cases of a zero leaf, a label-2 leaf, an internal label 2, and four unit labels exhaust all possibilities. Only the two extreme universal defenders survive for n at least four. The n=2 and n=3 cases are finite exact case analyses, and the standalone checker confirms all minima through n=7.

value.rationale: Half graphs are the canonical twin-free chain graphs and a standard test family for nested-neighborhood domination phenomena. The theorem gives the exact optimum and every optimizer, including a sharp uniqueness threshold at n=4, and it simultaneously determines the quasi-total strong differential by the published Gallai correspondence. The result is structural and family-wide rather than a small numerical instance.
